title: What Comes at Dusk
logline: As the light goes at the edge of a village, a ritual specialist and a family build an offering stand for a sick relative, and the whole village stays up with them until dawn.
human_question: What does a community do for someone in trouble that medicine alone cannot reach?

premise.story: A night-long healing ritual (thovil) held for a sick member of a family, from building the offering stands at dusk to the ceremony's end at dawn.
premise.place: A rural village compound in the low-country south.
premise.experience: Drums and masks in torchlight, offerings placed at the village's edge, a community keeping watch through the night, and the family's own hope, spoken or unspoken.

concept_links.why: The source itself connects one class of rebirth it describes to the beings who accept exactly these kinds of offerings [C053-M:L15]. It is one of the few places where the text points directly at a living Sri Lankan practice, and the film can simply watch that practice without asserting anything about the beings it names.

The source places various downcast and lesser spirits within its picture of the planes of existence [C051-P:L95-L101]. A ritual addressed to unseen beings is where that picture is actually lived, not studied.

what_camera_could_observe: The community gathering and staying through the night
what_must_be_real: A ritual the family and specialist have genuinely chosen to hold, for their own reasons, with the sick person's own consent where they are able to give it. The film asserts nothing about the cause of the illness.

possible_arc.opening: The offering stands going up as the light fails.
possible_arc.turn: The ceremony itself, deep in the night.
possible_arc.ending_open: Dawn, and whatever the family says or does not say about whether it helped.

requirements: A family and ritual specialist willing to have a real ceremony filmed
Full, ongoing consent from the sick person or their guardians, and from every performer
The sick person's dignity and privacy protected throughout

suggestions.name: A rural village in the Southern Province low country
suggestions.why: Thovil and related healing ceremonies remain a living low-country practice; no specific village identified.
suggestions.verify: No family, specialist or ceremony confirmed.

risks: Implying the illness was caused by past action or by anyone's fault
The sick person becoming a spectacle rather than the centre of care
Never asserting whether the beings addressed exist
drop_if: Full consent cannot be secured from the sick person or their family
The ceremony's meaning cannot be respectfully filmed without exposing the family's privacy

connections.note: Both are about a community's care reaching toward beings that ordinary comfort cannot reach directly, one for the newly dead, one for the endangered living.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
